questions.question: Describe the role of ion transport in maintaining the resting potential of a neurone (4 marks).
questions.answer: The Na+/K+ pump uses ATP to move 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in; K+ leaks out more readily than Na+ leaks in, so the inside is negative.
steps: The sodium-potassium pump uses ATP (active transport) to move 3 Na+ out of the axon for every 2 K+ moved in.

The membrane is more permeable to K+ (K+ leak channels), so K+ diffuses out down its gradient more than Na+ diffuses in.
Loss of positive ions from inside leaves the inside negative relative to the outside, giving a resting potential of about -70 mV.

questions.question: Compare and contrast the function of a sensory neurone and a motor neurone (3 marks).
questions.answer: Both carry impulses along axons; sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS, while motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors.
steps: Both types of neurone transmit electrical impulses (action potentials) along their axons.
Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors towards the CNS.

Sensory neurones have a cell body in a dorsal root ganglion and motor neurones have their cell body in the CNS, which is a structural contrast.

questions.question: Suggest why a person with Guillain-Barre syndrome has the symptoms of this disorder, where the immune system damages the myelin sheath of neurones (3 marks).
questions.answer: Damage to myelin slows or stops impulse conduction in sensory and motor neurones, so sensation, movement control and reflexes are lost.
steps: Myelin damage removes saltatory conduction, so impulses are slowed or fail to be transmitted.
Sensory impulses from the limbs cannot reach the brain, so sensation is lost.
Motor impulses cannot reach the muscles efficiently, so steadiness when walking is lost.
Reflex arcs cannot transmit impulses quickly enough, so reflexes such as the knee jerk are lost.

questions.question: Explain how mutations in genes coding for voltage-gated calcium ion channels might cause neurological conditions (4 marks).

A mutation can change the channel so it opens less or more than normal, or fails to close.
Abnormal Ca2+ entry changes neurotransmitter release, disrupting synaptic transmission and causing the condition.

questions.question: Describe how the pupil of an eye dilates and contracts in response to changes in light intensity (4 marks).
